browser: Installed stable Google Chrome 156 (headless, temporary profile) driven over the DevTools protocol; trusted keyboard, mouse and touch events only; visible DOM text and screenshots read; no game state read or injected; no Playwright.

observed: Player and key sprites were about 8 px tall on desktop and 4 px on the phone canvas; EXIT was untranslated in Chinese; gear-to-bridge linkage was barely visible; the upper half was mostly empty. Sent to owner as confirmed findings.
Larger actors, localized exit sign, overhead brass rods with letter badges mapping each gear to its bridges. Machine 1 cleared for 1200 in Chinese.
Runner about 12 px tall on desktop and 5 px on phone; RELAY label drawn under the runner; chalk marks and footprints faint.
2x camera zoom made the runner clear, but jump apexes pushed landing roofs to the bottom edge.
Replaying the owner's course-2 frame-exact route in real time failed: climbs needed near frame-exact timing. Sent as a blocking human-tolerance finding.
Kick grace and one-kick canyons made courses 1-2 winnable with tolerant cues, but the course-3 canyon camera left the runner off-screen while rising and falling.
Host status line showed only the genre because getState().status was a flight-data object; objective banner overlapped the HUD; phone HUD text too small.
Bilingual status and three-line HUD fixed. Holding Space when 'Hold Space to flare' first appeared stalled the wing on the approach and hard-landed; crash text blamed speed instead of sink rate.

A driver obeying only the visible status text lost course-1 attempts: 'Hold Space to flare' and 'Slow! Lower the nose' alternated every 0.2-0.8 s and the glider floated to the course edge; 'Course edge: turn back' named no key.
Text-only flight won (2748) with courses 1-2 clean, but course 3 lost two attempts: a missed-gate prompt with no key, and a flare cue while still banked.
New 'Too fast: hold Up' cue drove the wing into stall, cycling 'Too fast' and 'STALL' about once a second; course 2 lost an attempt.

Full English keyboard campaign won for 4100: three machines at 1200 each plus 100 per remaining life with all five lives. The ferry carried the player and key; a shared gear extended bridge B while lowering lift A; in Master Clockwork lift B rose while press C dropped onto the island behind the player.

Pressing Z away from the door's 40 px reach drops the key, and the bottom prompt shows which action is in reach. Two tester route errors (walking short of a deck before cranking; jumping before the crate) were recovered by recalling the platform and retaking the key.

Inputs on the win screen left score and status unchanged. R restarted at 0 with best 4100. Five deliberate pit falls each cost a life and rewound the machine; the fifth reached the explicit loss, which ignored further input.

Chinese 390x844 portrait: no horizontal overflow; all five touch controls fit; touch took the key and turned the gear, and the ferry carried the player across. 844x390 landscape fullscreen places movement and action controls in side columns; touch movement worked.
limitations: Emulated phone layouts and dispatched touch; no physical device or audio check.
The player accelerates gradually, so short taps under-walk; this is a feel note, not a defect.

observed: Full English keyboard campaign won for 1672 with all 4 lives: Gutter Row (roof hops and a chalk wall), Antenna Canyon (Left+X chalk climb, one kick across, roof hops, run-up wall-run of the final tower) and Skyline Relay (slick walls, canyon exit onto the right chalk, slick-based tower).

Momentum for a wall-run comes from the approach: a standing start at the tower edge clung and slid back (a fall cost one life and returned to the pad), while a run-up from the back of the pad ran the tower. The runner stayed visible below the HUD in every captured frame on this build.
Win screen ignored further input. R restarted at 0 with best 1672; four deliberate falls reached the explicit loss, which ignored input.

Chinese 390x844 portrait: no horizontal overflow, four touch controls; course 1 was completed entirely with multi-touch Right + Wall-run + Jump. 844x390 landscape fullscreen places controls in side columns.
limitations: Played with pause-and-inspect segments; edge jumps reward a visible run-up. Emulated touch and phone layouts only.
Driver note: real-time replays of frame-exact route strings drift in headless Chrome, so segment play was used for acceptance.

observed: Final source 3bb070ee (prompt-only guard added after 82254e12): re-flown in full with the same text-only driver and won 2785 with zero attempts lost; gate 3 missed on Needle Crest and recovered via 'Gate 3 missed: Hold Left: turn back'. Courses 1-2 were also clean in a Chinese-language run. The observations below were made on 82254e12, whose physics and courses are identical.

Full English campaign won for 2809 with no attempts lost by a driver that reads only the page status text every 0.15 s and presses the key it names (flare, hold Left, steer Left/Right, hold Up, stall Down). Thermal LIFT ribbons, gate poles and the minimap guided climbs and gates; courses 1 and 2 landed on the first approach.
On Needle Crest the glider missed gate 3; 'Gate 3 missed: Hold Left: turn back' led it back through the gate without losing an attempt. No corrective-prompt cycling was observed.

Win screen ignored input; R restarted at 0 with best 2809. Holding the nose down for the whole run still landed course 1, then missed gate 2 on course 2 twice and reached 'Out of attempts'; the loss screen ignored input.

Chinese 390x844 portrait: no horizontal overflow; five touch controls; holding the bank-left touch control changed course and the prompt asked to steer right. 844x390 landscape fullscreen places pitch and bank/flare controls in side columns.
limitations: Course 1 is forgiving: hands-off or nose-down flight can still land it.
Emulated touch and phone layouts; no physical device or audio check.
